statement: Use a small canonical binary encoding, not a runtime-defined serializer. Every canonical record has a 16-byte header: record_type u16, version u16, flags u32, payload_length u64, then payload.
Record payloads are ordered TLV fields: tag u16, type u8, flags u8, value_length u64, value.
TLV tags strictly increasing; flags and reserved bytes zero; integers big-endian; booleans exactly 00 or 01; strings UTF-8.
Sequences carry an explicit u64 item count followed by length-delimited items (item_length u64 then item). Maps are not used anywhere in the encoding.
Readers reject non-minimal, out-of-order, duplicate, unknown, or ill-typed TLV fields (fail closed).
research_needed: Differential fuzzing that mutates each rejection class and confirms rejection.

statement: The term non-minimal is undefined for fixed-width integers, and no TLV type-code table is given (vectors imply 1=u8, 3=u32, 4=u64, 7=32-byte digest, 8=UTF-8 string). An independent reader cannot be built from this text alone.

Planner v1 zstandard/v1 plan identifiers follow zstandard-v1-level-{level}-window-20; parameters are a closed 12-byte value: ZP01, level i32be, window_log u8, checksum u8, content_size u8, dictionary_id u8.
Planner v1 requires window log 20, checksum 0, content size 1, dictionary ID 0, no dictionary, no preceding transforms; readers reject any other parameter shape rather than consulting codec defaults.

statement: New filesystem archives use versioned normalized CDC chunking while historical archives retain fixed-1mib/v1 chunking.
Ordered Chunk references already represent arbitrary boundaries, so CDC and deduplication need no wire change.
Codec selection and chunking are physical choices, not Entry semantics.

Planner v3 may record canonical dictionary-backed ZD01 or bounded-prefix ZX01 parameter values while keeping codec identifier zstandard/v1; the frozen construction lives in cross-file-compression-v1.md.
Required incompatibility bit 0x2 (codec-transform-v1) enables first-class TransformStep records plus registered lz4/v1 and lzma2/v1 plans, without altering frozen v1-v3 plan interpretation.
Required bit 0x4 (reconstructive-transform-v1) requires bits 0x1 and 0x2, selects TransformStep v2 records, and adds the RECONSTRUCTION_DATA section.
Required bit 0x8 (whole-object-reconstruction-v1) requires 0x1, 0x2, and 0x4; selects TransformStep v3 and Chunk frame v3; adds the RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS section.
Required bit 0x10 (stream-layout-v1) requires no other bit, changes no record schema, only physical organization and access capability, and is declared exactly when layout discriminant is 2.
Feature chain forces reconstruction (0x4, 0x8, e.g. JPEG) to also declare cross-file compression (0x1) and codec-transform (0x2); no rationale for this coupling is given.
research_needed: Analyse whether reconstruction records actually depend on dictionary/group sections; reader-complexity cost of coupled tiers.
decision_needed: Should reconstruction features be decoupled from cross-file-compression in the frozen feature model?

statement: Cryptographic architecture is frozen and the encrypted-INDEXED subset implemented, with required bits 0x20 encrypted-indexed, 0x40 payload-suite, 0x80 recipient-xwing, 0x100 recipient-password, 0x200 signature-ed25519, 0x400 crypto-padding, 0x800 keyed-boundary-phte, 0x1000 private-resource-declaration.
Readers accept crypto bits only through the crypto-v1 INDEXED reader; 0x200 is accepted exactly when a nonempty authenticated EBCS kind-7 signature collection is present.
Canonical crypto records, feature constraints, and footer v2 are frozen in crypto-wire-v1.md; primitive and security rules are in crypto-suite-v1.md. This document does not itself define footer v2.

statement: Each INDEXED section starts with a 64-byte header: EBS1, section_type u16, version u16, flags u32, reserved u32, payload_length u64, SHA-256(payload), 8 reserved bytes.

Base schema sections occur exactly once in order DESCRIPTOR(1), TRANSFORM_PLANS(2), CHUNK_DATA(3), MANIFEST_RECORDS(4), FIDELITY(5), optional INDEX(6); unknown, missing, duplicate, or reordered authoritative sections are non-canonical; sections exist only in INDEXED.
Section type numbers are renumbered per feature set (CHUNK_DATA is 3, 5, 6, or 7; INDEX is 6, 8, 9, or 10) instead of stable type IDs, so interpreting a section type requires the feature bits.
research_needed: Assess tooling/independent-reader error risk; compare stable-ID designs.
decision_needed: Should v1 freeze stable section type identifiers independent of feature set?

statement: Bit 0x1 (cross-file-compression-v1) selects schema DESCRIPTOR(1), TRANSFORM_PLANS(2), DICTIONARIES(3), CHUNK_GROUPS(4), CHUNK_DATA(5), MANIFEST_RECORDS(6), FIDELITY(7), optional INDEX(8); both new sections occur exactly once even when empty.

Unencrypted reader recognizes bits 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10, 0x8000, 0x10000, 0x2000, 0x4000; crypto-v1 INDEXED reader additionally recognizes implemented crypto bits; all readers reject every other unknown required bit.
research_needed: Conformance corpus exercising every bit and unknown bits per reader.

statement: Bit 0x2 changes only the TransformPlan field-3 item schema and may be combined with 0x1, as planner v4 does.

With 0x4 the schema is DESCRIPTOR(1), TRANSFORM_PLANS(2), DICTIONARIES(3), CHUNK_GROUPS(4), RECONSTRUCTION_DATA(5), CHUNK_DATA(6), MANIFEST_RECORDS(7), FIDELITY(8), optional INDEX(9); RECONSTRUCTION_DATA occurs exactly once even when empty.

With 0x8 the schema adds RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS(6) after RECONSTRUCTION_DATA(5), then CHUNK_DATA(7), MANIFEST_RECORDS(8), FIDELITY(9), optional INDEX(10); both reconstruction sections occur exactly once even when empty.
CHUNK_DATA is a sequence of digest-ordered plan-driven frames: EBCH, version u16, flags u16, stored_length u64, chunk_id 32 bytes, logical_length u64, plan_ref u64, stored_bytes.

statement: Under cross-file-compression-v1, version-2 frames append group_ref (32 bytes) before stored bytes; zero means no group; it is the sole membership authority (ChunkGroups hold no member lists); frame order is the authority for preceding-Chunk dependencies.

Under whole-object-reconstruction-v1 frame version is 3; flag bit 0 marks a region-owned Chunk declaration with zero stored length, plan ref zero, no group, whose digest and logical length stay authoritative; other flag bits reserved zero.

The 128-byte INDEXED footer: magic, total container length, absolute offset/length pairs for DESCRIPTOR and MANIFEST_RECORDS, actual entry count, total logical bytes, SHA-256 of the entire preamble, 32 zero reserved bytes.
The INDEXED footer has no checksum over itself and binds only the preamble digest; detection of corrupted footer locators or totals relies on downstream section/identity checks.
research_needed: Fault-injection on footer bytes to confirm every corruption is detected and localized with a precise diagnostic.
decision_needed: Should the footer carry a self-checksum or section-directory digest?

statement: The STREAM footer keeps the same magic and width but declares the DESCRIPTOR item locator, STREAM_BODY extent, final actual Chunk, entry, and logical-byte totals, preamble digest, and STREAM_BODY digest.
Descriptor v1 (type 1/version 1) fields: namespace(1), identity profile(2), digest algorithm(3), planner ID(4), chunker ID(5), LAI(6), PCR(7), AUX(8).

Descriptor v2 (type 1/version 2) keeps v1 fields 1-8 and adds decode window(9), working set(10), decode flags(11), entry count(12), total logical bytes(13), max single-entry logical bytes(14), max expansion ratio milli(15), Chunk count(16), max path depth(17), max metadata bytes(18), max key-derivation cost(19).
TransformPlan (type 2) fields: plan ID(1), identifier(2), transform sequence(3), codec(4), parameters(5), optional dictionary(6), decode window(7), working set(8), flags(9).
Entry v1 (type 3) fields: LogicalPath components(1), kind(2), ContentRef kind(3), optional logical digest(4), MetadataSet(5), identity digest(6), auxiliary digest(7).

Entry v2 (type 3/version 2) fields: LogicalPath components(1), explicit kind(2), optional File content digest(3), optional Symlink target encoding(4) and bytes(5), MetadataItem-v2 sequence(6), identity digest(7), auxiliary digest(8).
Entry v3 (type 3/version 3) = Entry v2 fields 1-8, adds kind 4 ReparsePoint and optional canonical WindowsReparsePointV1 bytes(9).

Entry records store derived identity and auxiliary digests alongside the fields they summarize; the document does not state that readers recompute and compare them, only that authoritative records are re-encoded.
research_needed: Check reader for recomputation of per-Entry digests; mutation tests.
decision_needed: Are per-Entry stored digests verified on read, and is storing them necessary?

statement: ContentObject (type 4) fields: logical digest(1), chunk root(2), ordered Chunk references(3).
FidelityReport (type 5): captured(1), unavailable(2), degraded(3), platform(4), filesystem declarations(5). Fidelity issue (type 10): class(1), reason(2), optional entry scope(3).
Index entry (type 6) fields: Chunk digest(1), absolute frame offset(2), stored length(3).
PathComponent (type 7) carries an explicit encoding(1) and exact bytes(2); LogicalPath is a sequence of such components.
MetadataItem v1 (type 8) fields: name(1), criticality(2), restorability(3), and either boolean(4) or timestamp(5).

MetadataItem v2 (type 8/version 2): registered name ID(1), optional criticality(2), restorable disposition(3), and exactly one of bool(4), Timestamp(5), u32(6), digest(7), XAttr sequence(8), SparseMap(9), selected by a closed registry.
MetadataItem v3 (type 8/version 3) extends the v2 registry with ACL sequence(10), WindowsSecurityDescriptor bytes(11), WindowsReparsePoint bytes(12); timestamp/u32 fields reused by closed name IDs.
Timestamp (type 9) fields: signed seconds(1), nanoseconds(2), source precision(3), restorable(4).
Dictionary (type 11) fields: dictionary digest(1), codec(2), format(3), construction(4), exact bytes(5).
ChunkGroup (type 12) fields: group ID(1), maximum lookback Chunks(2), maximum preceding logical bytes(3).

TransformStep (type 13): identifier(1), canonical parameters(2). TransformStep v2 (type 15) adds optional reconstruction reference(3). TransformStep v3 (type 17) adds optional ReconstructionData reference(3).

Record evolution convention is inconsistent: TransformStep v2/v3 and ReconstructionAudit v2 get new type numbers (15, 17, 19), while Descriptor, Entry, and MetadataItem revisions reuse the type with a version field.
decision_needed: Which record-evolution convention (new type vs version field) is normative for future records?

statement: ReconstructionData (type 14): exact-byte digest(1), format/version(2), intermediate length(3), exact reconstruction bytes(4). ReconstructionFallback (type 16): Chunk digest(1), fallback reason enum(2).

ReconstructionRegion (type 18) has 13 fields: region identity, ContentObject, start Chunk index, Chunk count, plan ref, logical bytes, transformed bytes, access logical bytes, access Chunks, worst reconstructed bytes, encoded representation, ordinary physical bytes, region overhead bytes.
ReconstructionAudit v2 (type 19) fields: target kind(1), target digest(2), transform identifier(3), reason(4).

ConversionProvenance (type 28) fields: source format, adapter ID, source SHA-256, import mode, source entry count, observation count, Omission/Refinement/Divergence/Irreconcilable counts, ordered resolutions, synthesized ancestor paths, unsupported metadata classes, outcome (14 fields).
ConversionResolution (type 29) fields: conflict class(1), semantic field(2), authorities(3), observed values(4), action(5).

ConversionResolution type 29 appears twice in the record table (once plain, once nested-only) with different field-3 names (authorities vs authority names); unclear whether they are one schema or two.
research_needed: Compare against code schema.
decision_needed: Is type 29 nested-only, and what is the exact field-3 type?

statement: LegacyPreservation (type 30) embeds preservation format, source format, source SHA-256, exact source bytes, ordered observations, conflicts, selected resolutions; nested types 31-36 encode PreservedObservation, Conflict, Authority, Value, Location, LOMResolution.
research_needed: Measure archive size overhead of embedding exact source bytes.

statement: XAttrV1 (37): exact name bytes, exact value bytes. SparseMapV1 (38): logical file size, ordered SparseExtent sequence. SparseExtentV1 (39): offset, nonzero length.
AclV1 (40): dialect, scope, ordered AclEntryV1 sequence. AclEntryV1 (41): ACE type, principal form, optional numeric ID, optional UUID, permissions, flags.
WindowsSecurityDescriptorV1 (42) holds exact validated self-relative descriptor bytes; WindowsReparsePointV1 (43) holds a nonzero tag and an exact bounded payload (bound value not given here).

statement: Without codec-transform-v1, TransformPlan field 3 is the historical empty sequence; with it, every item is a v1 type-13 TransformStep. Non-empty legacy string placeholders were never emitted by frozen planners and are rejected.

With reconstructive-transform-v1, every field-3 item is a type-15 TransformStep v2; type 13 never reinterpreted; structural steps omit field 3; the sole reconstructive step must be first and carries one digest reference to a type-14 ReconstructionData.

Type-16 fallback records follow all type-14 records in RECONSTRUCTION_DATA, ordered by Chunk digest, as non-authoritative creation-audit data; reason 1 = recognition or mandatory exact verification failed, reason 2 = verified candidate lost the complete-cost comparison.
Non-authoritative creation-audit records (types 16, 19) sit inside authoritative sections; unclear whether they must be canonical/deterministic across producers and whether they affect only PCI.
research_needed: Check whether identical EAM + planner yields identical audit records on different machines.
decision_needed: Should audit data live in authoritative sections, and must it be deterministic?

statement: With whole-object-reconstruction-v1, TransformPlan sequences contain type-17 steps; a self-contained reconstructive step omits field 3; type-18 regions precede type-19 audits in RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS, both canonical and uniquely ordered; region membership is not repeated as a list.
Entries are in canonical LogicalPath order; ContentObjects, Chunks, TransformPlans, and Index entries are ordered by identifiers; set-like string and fidelity lists are sorted and unique.
The reader re-encodes authoritative records and rejects any representation that is not byte-canonical.
research_needed: Fuzzing for accepted non-canonical encodings; independent reader parity.

statement: Chunk and ContentObject logical digests are plain SHA-256 over exact plaintext bytes; section digests, feature checksum, preamble binding, and PCI are plain SHA-256 over the exact bytes named.
Structured hash = SHA-256 of prefix, u64be domain length, domain, u64be field count, then each field as u64be length plus bytes.

Spec renders the structured-hash prefix with a doubled backslash inside a text code block, readable as literal backslash characters; code uses a NUL terminator (identity.rs:29 b"Entrybound hash v1\0"). Independent implementers could compute wrong hashes.
refines_or_supersedes: code crates/entrybound/src/identity.rs:29 differs in rendering from docs/format-v0.md L380
evidence_in_source: cross-check of doc against code by this agent
research_needed: Publish structured-hash test vectors; correct doc text.
decision_needed: Fix the spec to state the NUL byte explicitly and add vectors?

statement: Domains used: chunk-tree/{leaf,empty,node}, entry/{identity,aux}/v1, manifest/{leaf,empty,node}, lai/v1, pcr/v1, aux-manifest/{leaf,empty,node}, fidelity/v1, conversion/absent/v1, conversion/provenance/v1, aux/v1.
Domain list may be incomplete: no domains are listed for legacy preservation, POSIX/security metadata digests, or crypto transcripts, and no structured-hash test vectors appear in this slice.
research_needed: Grep code for all domain labels and compare with spec.
decision_needed: Is the domain label registry exhaustive and where is it normative?

statement: Entry identity binds identity profile, component bytes and encodings, kind, ContentRef kind, logical digest, and core.executable.
research_needed: Cross-platform study: platforms without an executable bit (Windows) and identity stability when importing from them.
decision_needed: Should core.executable be identity-bearing (LAI) rather than AUX?

statement: Entry AUX binds every remaining implemented metadata item (mtime, POSIX topology, ACLs, exact Windows security/platform metadata, macOS flags/birthtime); ReparsePoint tag/data and Symlink target remain LAI facts.
LAI binds SHA-256, manifest root, identity/v1 profile, Complete role, entry count, and total logical size.

PCR binds SHA-256, the digest-ordered (logical_digest, chunk_root) list, unique physical Chunk count, and chunker ID; transform plans are deliberately excluded so recompression with unchanged chunking preserves PCR.

PCR excludes TransformPlans, Dictionaries, and reconstruction data, so a signature over PCR does not authenticate codec choice or decode path; security implications of signed physical binding are not discussed.
research_needed: Threat analysis: substitution of transform plans/dictionaries in signed archives (decompression bombs, reconstruction attacks).
decision_needed: What exactly does a PCR signature attest, and must decode-path records be signed?

statement: AUX binds SHA-256, the Entry-AUX Merkle root, FidelityReport digest, and either the explicit absent-ConversionRecord digest or the canonical ConversionProvenance digest.
PCI is SHA-256 over every exact .eb byte and changes when an Index is added, removed, or repaired even though LAI, PCR, and AUX do not.
Native archive file extension is .eb.
research_needed: Check extension collisions with existing software and OS associations.
decision_needed: Is .eb final and will a media type be registered?

statement: A validated EAM encoded under both layouts gives identical LAI, PCR, AUX and different PCI; no logical identity binds layout, Chunk frame order, Index, or codec choice.
research_needed: Property tests over corpora comparing roots across layouts and codecs.

statement: STREAM selects object-major frame order, so ContentStore::physical_order differs from the INDEXED encoding of the same model; that field is physical only and participates in no identity.
format-v0 states PCR equality across layouts unconditionally, whereas stream-layout-v1 qualifies PCR equality with 'when chunk organization is unchanged'; the precise condition is unclear.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md §Identity equivalence L402 narrows docs/format-v0.md L411
research_needed: Test whether any STREAM encoding path can alter chunking.
decision_needed: Can STREAM encoding ever alter chunk organization, and if so is PCR equality a guaranteed invariant?

statement: Crypto v1 is INDEXED-only and uses one non-negotiated PayloadSuite: AES-256-GCM-SIV, HKDF-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-256, and SHA-256.
research_needed: External cryptographic review; performance of AES-GCM-SIV without AES-NI; crypto agility path.

statement: A random 32-byte archive file key feeds a labeled key hierarchy.
research_needed: RNG source audit per platform.

statement: A separate HMAC commitment is verified before a candidate file key is accepted (key commitment).
research_needed: Formal analysis of commitment against partitioning-oracle/multi-key attacks.

statement: Record/segment associated data, mandatory segment endings, and an encrypted terminal archive-final record are claimed to bind order, truncation, identities, recipient set, and the fixed footer.
research_needed: Formal/symbolic model of AD construction; truncation/reorder/splice fault-injection tests.

statement: Normal public-key recipients use the draft-10 X-Wing construction (ML-KEM-768 + X25519).
research_needed: Track X-Wing draft to RFC changes; interop vectors against other implementations; ML-KEM crate audit status.
decision_needed: How will archives handle divergence between X-Wing draft-10 and the final RFC?

statement: Password-only archives use Argon2id and cannot mix with hybrid public-key recipients.
research_needed: Usability study of password-vs-recipient exclusivity; Argon2id parameter cost on low-end devices.
decision_needed: Is forbidding mixed password and public-key recipients acceptable for v1 users?

statement: Names, metadata, manifest, Index, identities, decode budgets, and embedded signatures are encrypted; only format/crypto discovery, CryptoEnvelope, recipient method framing, padded ciphertext framing, and fixed footer remain public.
research_needed: Leakage audit of public fields (sizes, recipient counts, feature bits) on real archives.

statement: Encrypted STREAM is deferred and must fail closed; it remains unsupported.
research_needed: Design and security analysis of streaming AEAD with no-seek writer and private footer-located descriptor.
decision_needed: Is encrypted STREAM (e.g. piped encrypted backups) required for v1?

statement: Default encrypted creation uses authenticated quarter-octave record padding and a secret-derived Gear table as defense in depth.
research_needed: Measure size overhead of quarter-octave padding; empirical boundary-leakage attacks against secret Gear tables.

statement: A separately declared PHTE + AES-128 keyed-boundary mode supplies the stronger published keyed-CDC construction.
evidence_in_source: reference to published construction (not cited here)
research_needed: Verify published construction's security proof applies to the implemented parameters; throughput and dedup-ratio cost vs secret Gear.

statement: The weaker secret-Gear boundary mode is the default while PHTE is described as stronger; no performance or ratio data justifying the default appears here.
research_needed: Benchmark PHTE vs secret Gear (speed, dedup ratio) and quantify leakage difference.
decision_needed: Should PHTE keyed boundaries be the default for encrypted archives?

statement: Neither padding/boundary mode claims to hide total archive size or access patterns.
research_needed: User-facing documentation testing whether users understand the residual leakage.

statement: In encrypted archives exact dedup remains plaintext-SHA-256 equality within one archive/file-key domain only.
Convergent or cross-tenant encryption is forbidden.
Ed25519 signatures preserve independent content (LAI, AUX, identity profile, format), physical (PCR), and addressing (suite, recipient-set digest, commitment, archive ID) bindings.
research_needed: Usability and semantics study of what each binding means to verifiers; misbinding analysis.
decision_needed: How are the separate binding classes presented to users as trust decisions?

statement: Transcript encodings, feature assignments, limits, vectors, and reason codes are normative in crypto-wire-v1.md; threat model and review record in crypto-threat-model-v1.md and crypto-review-v1.md; implemented subset recorded in crypto-implementation-v1.md.
Detached type-26 signature records and encrypted embedded signatures are operational.
Crypto architecture is declared frozen with an internal review record; no independent external security review is established by this document.
research_needed: Independent third-party cryptographic and implementation audit.
decision_needed: Is an external audit required before declaring crypto v1 stable?

statement: Implementation exposed a frozen-wire contradiction: Descriptor v1 cannot encode the private ResourceBudget and DecodeRequirements crypto v1 requires; Descriptor type 1/version 2 is the single-authority correction.

Descriptor v2 tags 1-8 match v1 and required tags 9-19 encode the two declarations; new encrypted INDEXED writers set feature 0x1000 and emit v2; unencrypted INDEXED/STREAM writers remain byte-frozen on Descriptor v1.
The public encrypted preamble carries all-zero privacy sentinels for budgets/decode requirements, not a competing declaration.
research_needed: DoS analysis: reader resource use before decryption reveals budgets; caller-policy defaults.
decision_needed: How do readers bound resources on encrypted archives before the private descriptor is decrypted?

statement: Pre-correction encrypted Descriptor-v1 archives remain explicitly labelled legacy experimental compatibility input.
decision_needed: Will v1 readers keep accepting pre-correction encrypted Descriptor-v1 archives, and until when?

location: §Encrypted INDEXED cryptographic extension L453-463; §Transform and chunking L196
statement: Frozen crypto wire has already been corrected twice after freeze (EBPO/EBCS grammars, Descriptor v2); the discipline governing further post-freeze corrections before v1 is not stated.
decision_needed: What change-control process governs corrections to frozen wire elements before and after v1?

statement: The Index exists only in INDEXED; STREAM has none by design and readers report it as not applicable rather than absent or invalid.

Index entries hold only physical Chunk-frame locators; the reader always rebuilds the authoritative locator map by scanning CHUNK_DATA and uses a present Index only if section digest, canonical encoding, and full locator map match.
refines_or_supersedes: narrowed for random readers by docs/format-v0.md L58-62

statement: Index diagnostics: EB_ECF_INDEX_INVALID_REBUILT for a mismatching Index and EB_ECF_INDEX_ABSENT_REBUILT for an absent one; neither changes EAM interpretation.
Native tooling v1 adds no wire records or feature bits.
Representation-only repack preserves LAI, AUX, and PCR while layout and Index changes affect only the container; explicit v6 replanning preserves LAI/AUX and may change PCR.
research_needed: Repack round-trip tests across layouts and planners.

statement: Inspection and diff reports are external versioned JSON documents and are not archive semantic authorities.
decision_needed: What stability guarantees apply to inspection/diff JSON schemas?

statement: STREAM layout document is an experimental implementation note for the second physical ECF layout and not a frozen Entrybound v1 specification.
decision_needed: When is stream-layout-v1 frozen as part of the v1 specification?

statement: STREAM is a second physical organization of the same EAM; it writes to a sink implementing only std::io::Write and reads from a source implementing only std::io::Read.
STREAM and INDEXED differ only in physical organization and access capability and never disagree about meaning; one validated EAM yields identical LAI, PCR, AUX under both; only PCI differs.
research_needed: Cross-layout differential tests over large corpora, including all feature combinations.

statement: Bit 0x10 is a required incompatibility feature; readers lacking it must refuse rather than read STREAM bytes as INDEXED sections; layout discriminant 2 makes historical readers fail closed twice (unknown bit and unknown layout).
research_needed: Test historical reader builds against STREAM archives.

statement: The 0x10 bit and layout 2 are declared together or not at all; declaring one without the other is non-canonical.
STREAM composes with existing required bits, adds no ordering constraints beyond theirs, and requires none of them.

This document covers STREAM composition only with 0x1, 0x4, 0x8; composition with posix (0x8000), platform-security (0x10000), conversion-provenance (0x2000), and legacy-preservation (0x4000) features is not described.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L135-141, L255-258 (0x2000 valid for STREAM)
research_needed: Conformance tests of STREAM with every unencrypted feature bit.
decision_needed: Which feature bits are valid with STREAM, per a single composition matrix?

statement: Stale text: AUX is said to bind only the absent-ConversionRecord digest and STREAM is said to have no legacy adapters, while format-v0 permits conversion-provenance-v1 in STREAM with the provenance digest in AUX.
research_needed: Confirm STREAM import output with provenance in code/tests.
decision_needed: Can legacy import produce STREAM output with conversion provenance in v1?

statement: STREAM archives keep the .eb extension; layout is a container property, not a property of its name.
research_needed: User study: do users/tools need to distinguish seekable vs streaming archives by name or media type parameter?

statement: STREAM uses the same 256-byte preamble at the same offsets as INDEXED; layout is 2, offset 160 holds the declared dedup window, offset 176 footer-offset hint must be zero.
The footer hint is zero because a sequential writer cannot know its final extent and the STREAM footer is self-locating at EOF; hostility summary at offset 168 stays zero.
Magic, version, feature bitmaps and checksum, archive role, BudgetDeclared, decode requirements, and the eight ResourceBudget values are declared identically in both layouts.

Body shape: preamble; STREAM_BODY with TRANSFORM_PLANS, optional DICTIONARIES/CHUNK_GROUPS (0x1), RECONSTRUCTION_DATA (0x4), RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS (0x8), interleaved CHUNK_FRAMEs and ContentObject records, Entry records, FIDELITY, DESCRIPTOR; 128-byte self-locating footer.
STREAM_BODY carries no length at its beginning; its final extent is established by the footer.
Every body item begins with a fixed 16-byte header: EBI1, tag u16, version u16, flags u32, reserved u32; version is 1 and flags/reserved are zero.

Frozen item tags: 1 TRANSFORM_PLANS (always once), 2 DICTIONARIES and 3 CHUNK_GROUPS (once with 0x1), 4 RECONSTRUCTION_DATA (0x4), 5 RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS (0x8), 6 CHUNK_FRAME (per unique Chunk), 7 MANIFEST_RECORD (per Entry/ContentObject), 8 FIDELITY, 9 DESCRIPTOR (once each).
Unknown STREAM item tags are refused, never skipped.
decision_needed: Should any future STREAM items be skippable (e.g. advisory data), requiring a skippable-tag class?

statement: A record item declares payload length and payload digest once: item header, payload_length u64, SHA-256(payload), payload.

Each record item payload is byte-identical to the corresponding INDEXED section payload, except MANIFEST_RECORD carries exactly one type-3 Entry or type-4 ContentObject; concatenating MANIFEST_RECORD payloads in body order yields exactly the INDEXED MANIFEST_RECORDS payload.

If INDEXED MANIFEST_RECORDS uses canonical sequence encoding (count and item-length prefixes per format-v0 L364), plain concatenation of single-record payloads could not equal it; the exact MANIFEST_RECORDS framing and its record order are unclear.
research_needed: Compare byte layouts produced by both writers in code.
decision_needed: What is the exact byte framing and record order of INDEXED MANIFEST_RECORDS?

statement: A CHUNK_FRAME item body is an ordinary EBCH frame, byte-identical to the frame INDEXED places in CHUNK_DATA for the same Chunk.
The frame's own stored_length is the sole authority for its extent; neither the item nor any trailing record repeats it; the layout has no ZIP-style forward header plus trailing duplicate.
Frame version and flags follow INDEXED rules: version 3 with 0x8, version 2 with 0x1, else version 1; flag bit 0 marks a region-owned Chunk declaration with zero stored length.

CHUNK_FRAME items carry no item-level digest; stored bytes are decoded before any stored-byte integrity check (plaintext Chunk digest after decode; STREAM_BODY digest only at EOF), so codecs process unauthenticated input.
research_needed: Fuzz all codecs/reconstruction decoders with hostile frames under budgets; compare with INDEXED section-digest-first behaviour.
decision_needed: Should STREAM frames carry a stored-bytes digest checked before decoding?

statement: Supporting items come first, in tag order, each exactly once, with the required set determined by the declared features.
CHUNK_FRAME and MANIFEST_RECORD items interleave; a ContentObject record may appear only after every Chunk frame it references.
Entry records follow every ContentObject record; no CHUNK_FRAME and no ContentObject record may follow the first Entry record.
FIDELITY follows the manifest records and DESCRIPTOR is the last item.
ContentObject records are uniquely ordered by logical digest; Entry records are in canonical LogicalPath order; Chunk frame identities are unique.
Readers enforce item order while reading and refuse violating bodies; STREAM Chunk frames are not digest-ordered; canonical STREAM frame order is object-major.
INDEXED emits physical_order as the planner produced it and relies on the Index or a CHUNK_DATA scan for lookup.
research_needed: Check INDEXED writer ordering in code.

statement: STREAM selects a deterministic sequential organization: ContentObjects visited in canonical logical-digest order; for each, its not-yet-emitted Chunks are emitted, then its Manifest record.
A bounded-lookback ChunkGroup is emitted as one contiguous run where its first member is needed, preserving group relative order from physical_order and thus its exact stored bytes.
Any Chunk referenced by no ContentObject is emitted after the last object record.
The rule for unreferenced Chunks implies such Chunks can exist in a valid EAM; whether they are permitted, and how they count in PCR unique Chunk count and the dedup window, is unstated.
research_needed: Check EAM invariants in code for orphan Chunks.
decision_needed: Are unreferenced Chunks valid in a canonical archive?

statement: No semantic fact changes under STREAM organization: Chunk set, ContentObjects, Entries, declared bounds, and identities are unchanged, and bounded-lookback prefixes come from the same preceding members so prefix-coded Chunks decode identically.
research_needed: Property tests with groups interleaved across objects and shared Chunks; decode equality checks.

statement: Exact deduplication is not weakened for STREAM: a Chunk still appears exactly once and later ContentObjects reference it by identity.

With frame_index(c) the frame ordinal and S(o) the frames emitted before object o's run began, a reference with frame_index(c) < S(o) is a historical cross-object dedup reference of distance S(o) minus frame_index(c).
stream_dedup_window is the largest such distance in the archive (zero if none); objects becoming ready at the same frame count form one run sharing a single S(o).

Reader retains the current run's Chunks plus at most window older Chunks; run bounded by declared max_single_entry_logical_bytes and chunk_count, history by the window; group history is a separate smaller cache bounded by max_lookback and max_preceding_bytes.
research_needed: Measure peak reader memory on adversarial and real archives; check multi-object runs against single-entry bound.

statement: The window counts Chunks, not bytes; its byte bound depends on maximum Chunk size, which is not a declared ResourceBudget, and a run of several objects may exceed the single-entry bound.
research_needed: Compute worst-case bytes for window x max chunk under each chunker; hostile archive tests.
decision_needed: Should STREAM declare a byte-denominated retention bound or a maximum Chunk size?

statement: Producer CLI: --stream-window n refuses an organization needing more than n; --stream-window auto accepts whatever the organization needs.
Default for explicit STREAM packing is window 0, refusing any cross-object historical dependency.
research_needed: Corpus measurement of required windows; usability test of failure rate for typical directories with duplicate files.
decision_needed: Is a default of 0 (failing on any duplicate content) the right UX, versus auto with a bounded ceiling?

statement: --stream-window is a ceiling the producer commits to; the archive always declares the exact minimum its organization requires (ceiling 8 on an archive needing 1 declares 1).
If the plan cannot meet the ceiling, packing fails with EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED naming the required window; it never silently raises the window or rewrites plan semantics to fit.
The object-major logical-digest order is fixed rather than optimized, so the required window may be larger than an alternative deterministic order would need.
research_needed: Measure window distributions under alternative deterministic orders (e.g. path order, dedup-aware).
decision_needed: Should STREAM frame order be optimized to minimize the dedup window?

statement: Shared dictionaries do not create historical references (a dictionary is not a Chunk), while bounded-lookback ChunkGroups and files sharing content usually do, so such archives normally need auto or a non-zero ceiling.
research_needed: Corpus study of window requirements by data type.

statement: Reader tracks the same run boundaries and refuses references beyond the declared window (EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED); a reference to a Chunk whose frame was never seen is EB_ECF_STREAM_FORWARD_REFERENCE.
Reader validates the declared window only as an upper bound and does not require the tightest value.
Writers declare the exact minimum window but readers accept any upper bound, so several byte encodings of the same EAM are accepted, in tension with the byte-canonical re-encoding stance.
decision_needed: Should STREAM readers reject non-minimal declared windows as non-canonical?

statement: The fixed 128-byte STREAM trailer keeps the INDEXED footer magic and width and is self-locating in the last 128 bytes at EOF.

STREAM footer offsets: 0 magic; 8 intended total length; 16 DESCRIPTOR item offset; 24 DESCRIPTOR item length; 32 STREAM_BODY length; 40 final unique Chunk count; 48 entry count; 56 total logical bytes; 64 preamble SHA-256; 96 STREAM_BODY SHA-256.

DESCRIPTOR is footer-located because final identity roots and totals are known only at the end; it carries the INDEXED descriptor fields: namespace, identity profile, digest algorithm, planner ID, chunker ID, LAI, PCR, AUX.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/format-v0.md L458-459 (STREAM stays on Descriptor v1)

statement: Nothing already emitted is ever revisited, so the STREAM writer is valid against a Write-only sink, and the implementation is typed that way.
Truncation stays distinguishable from corruption: a source ending inside the preamble, an item, or before the fixed footer returns TRUNCATED EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM.
research_needed: Truncate-at-every-offset conformance tests.

statement: A complete footer declaring total length above bytes read is TRUNCATED; a declared length below bytes read, or bytes trailing a complete footer, is CORRUPT EB_ECF_INCORRECT_TOTAL_LENGTH.
A byte pattern at an item boundary that is neither an item header nor the footer magic is CORRUPT EB_ECF_STREAM_ITEM_ORDERING.

How a non-seeking reader recognizes a complete footer at a non-EOF position, or distinguishes truncation exactly at an item boundary from corruption, is not fully specified; classification of concatenated or appended archives is also unstated.
research_needed: Conformance corpus: truncation at each boundary, appended garbage, concatenated archives, fake footer magic inside items.
decision_needed: What exact state machine defines TRUNCATED vs CORRUPT for STREAM?

statement: Every decoder dependency (TransformPlans, Dictionaries, ChunkGroups, ReconstructionData, ReconstructionRegions) precedes the first CHUNK_FRAME, so discovering a codec, dictionary, group, or reconstruction method never requires seeking back.

For whole-object reconstruction regions the reader holds the region representation until its ContentObject record arrives, then reconstructs members and verifies each member Chunk against its declared digest before staging; the region stays one authoritative physical representation.
Memory held for region representations and reconstruction output while awaiting the ContentObject record is not tied to any declared budget in this document.
research_needed: Measure peak memory with large JPEG regions in STREAM; hostile region sizes.
decision_needed: Which declared bound limits held region state in STREAM?

statement: BudgetDeclared = true is the normal case: directory packing plans the whole archive, knows its totals, and declares them.
To declare budgets, the STREAM writer encodes its frames once to measure stored lengths before emitting the preamble, costing memory proportional to the encoded archive but never a seek.
research_needed: Measure writer peak memory on archives larger than RAM.
decision_needed: Should the writer spill pre-encoded frames to disk or use two passes to scale beyond RAM?

statement: BudgetDeclared = false: preamble ResourceBudget values all zero (non-zero is non-canonical); caller policy alone bounds decoding, enforced incrementally; final actual totals reported in footer; inspect reports no pre-payload budget.
Absence of a budget declaration never means unlimited resources.
There is no CLI option or current producer for BudgetDeclared = false, although readers fully support it.
research_needed: Conformance vectors exercising the undeclared-budget reader path, since no producer creates them.
decision_needed: Will an incremental/pipe-input producer that emits BudgetDeclared = false be shipped in v1?

statement: Library API: encode_stream<W: Write>(input: &Archive, options: StreamWriteOptions, sink: W) -> Result<StreamWriteSummary>.

The writer validates the EAM first, never seeks, emits deterministic bytes, enforces the requested window, computes footer and identity roots while writing, returns final identities and statistics; Seek is absent from the bound.
research_needed: Repeat-encode byte equality across platforms and thread counts.

statement: The INDEXED encoder remains available unchanged as encode.
Library API: open_stream_with_limits<R: Read>(source: R, limits: SequentialLimits) -> Result<SequentialArchive>.

The reader makes one front-to-back pass: validates framing, enforces caller resource policy, decodes and verifies each physical item on arrival, tracks bounded dependencies, accumulates manifest data, recomputes identity roots incrementally, and validates descriptor and footer at EOF.
The STREAM reader does not buffer the archive into a Vec and call the INDEXED reader, and never holds the whole archive in memory.
research_needed: Peak-RSS measurements on multi-GB STREAM archives under the Verify policy.

statement: SequentialLimits carries the caller's ResourceBudget, DecodeRequirements, staging limits, a largest-single-item bound, a largest-total-container bound, and the content policy; default values are not given.
research_needed: Derive safe defaults from corpora and hostile tests.
decision_needed: What default SequentialLimits does the CLI apply?

statement: StreamContentPolicy: Verify retains only the declared window (verify, list, inspect); Stage retains every Chunk in bounded staging (extraction); Retain places every Chunk back into the returned model (explain).
StreamAccessProfile reports random_entry_lookup false always, entry_cursor Sequential, listing_requires_full_scan true, source_replayable false.
No API may look random-access while hiding an O(n) scan; STREAM is never reported random-access merely because the source is seekable; the reader is chosen from the archive's declared layout.
Random entry lookup on STREAM is unavailable until the stream has been scanned or repacked.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/stream-layout-v1.md L422 says no repack command
decision_needed: Should a seekable STREAM file get an optional scan-and-cache random-access mode?

statement: Complexity: verify O(n) both; list O(entries) after open vs O(n) scan; inspect O(n) both; one entry by path O(1) locate + O(chunks) decode vs O(n) scan; extract all O(n) vs O(n) plus staging.
refines_or_supersedes: tension with docs/format-v0.md L470-471 (INDEXED reader always rebuilds locator map by scanning)
research_needed: Benchmarks of open/list/single-entry extraction for both layouts, local and remote.

statement: Because manifest records follow data, sequential extraction stages decoded content internally and creates nothing under the destination until the archive has fully verified.

Materialization begins only after framing, every Chunk digest, EAM invariants, identity roots, footer binding, and exact total length are established; unverified data never becomes a final extracted file.
Staging keeps a resident set up to StagingLimits::memory_bytes and spills the rest to a private temporary file; total_bytes bounds the whole store; archive plaintext is never required in RAM.
research_needed: Disk-full and total_bytes exhaustion behaviour; plaintext exposure of spill files for future encrypted STREAM.

statement: The staging temp file is the reader's own scratch space, created with create_new and never reachable through a caller-supplied path; seeking inside it is unrelated to the archive no-seek guarantee.
research_needed: Temp-directory attack review (shared tmp, permissions, symlink races) on each OS.

statement: Staging is released when the pass ends, including on failure and truncation.
research_needed: Test cleanup after process kill/crash, not only error returns.

statement: The destination stays capability-confined, existing objects are never overwritten, and extraction uses the same collision-refusing policy as INDEXED.

Full staging before materialization can require temporary disk roughly equal to extracted size and total_bytes may refuse large archives; no option for incremental materialization with quarantine is described.
research_needed: Measure staging disk overhead and failure rate for large STREAM extractions.
decision_needed: Should STREAM extraction offer verified-incremental or quarantine-directory materialization?

statement: ebound verify on STREAM checks preamble, feature model, item framing and order, stored lengths, supporting-record integrity, dedup-window constraints, Dictionaries and ChunkGroups, reconstruction dependencies and regions, plaintext Chunk digests, EAM invariants, LAI, PCR, AUX, footer binding, exact total length, and PCI.
verify is said to validate PCI, but PCI is not embedded in the archive, so it can only be computed, not compared, unless an external reference is supplied.
decision_needed: What does verify report for PCI and can users supply an expected PCI?

statement: Encoding the same planned EAM under both layouts: LAI equal, AUX equal, PCR equal when chunk organization is unchanged, PCI different.
LAI binds Entry manifest root, entry count, total logical size; PCR binds digest-ordered (logical_digest, chunk_root), unique Chunk count, chunker ID; none binds layout, frame order, Index, or codec.

Opening either encoding yields the same entries, ContentObjects, Chunks, Dictionaries, ChunkGroups, ReconstructionData, and ReconstructionRegions, and extraction yields identical file bytes; only ContentStore::physical_order differs.
research_needed: Differential open/extract tests across layouts for all feature combinations.

statement: No encrypted STREAM layout; the text says STREAM archives are unencrypted as INDEXED archives are in this bootstrap, which is stale now that encrypted INDEXED is implemented.
decision_needed: Is encrypted STREAM in scope for v1?

statement: STREAM has no random entry access, no partial extraction, and no repack command; any per-entry question requires a full scan.
refines_or_supersedes: possibly stale vs docs/format-v0.md L477-480 (repack with layout change)
research_needed: Check whether repack now accepts STREAM input.
decision_needed: Should repack from STREAM to INDEXED and partial extraction from STREAM be supported in v1?

statement: The source is consumed by the pass; answering a second question about a piped archive requires piping it again.
explain needs retained plaintext to re-derive the planner's alternatives; on STREAM it runs under the Retain policy, whose memory profile matches opening the INDEXED encoding.
research_needed: Measure explain memory on large STREAM archives.

statement: The writer takes an in-memory Archive, so writer memory is proportional to the archive; the format needs no seek but the current writer API is not an incremental producer.

statement: Vector file freezes historical Descriptor v1 bytes and defines corrected Descriptor v2 bytes from private-resource-declaration-v1 (0x1000); hex is lowercase and holds the complete canonical record.

This agent recomputed SHA-256 for all five vectors; each matches its declared digest. Sizes: DESCRIPTOR_V1 249 bytes (payload 233), DESCRIPTOR_V2 and V2_MAX 465 bytes (payload 449), each PUBLIC_CONTEXT 217 bytes.
research_needed: Check the reader/writer tests consume these vectors.

statement: Decoded TLV type codes in the Descriptor vectors: 1 for one-byte integers (identity profile, digest algorithm), 3 for u32 (decode flags), 4 for u64, 7 for 32-byte digests, 8 for UTF-8 strings; all TLV flags zero. No type-code table appears in format-v0.

statement: DESCRIPTOR_V1 example: namespace ecf/bootstrap-v1, identity profile code 1, digest algorithm code 1, planner ID balanced-v6, chunker ID gear-norm-v1, placeholder LAI/PCR/AUX of repeated 11, 22, 33 bytes; record type 1 version 1.

DESCRIPTOR_V2 example values: decode window 1 MiB, working set 2 MiB, decode flags 5, 3 entries, 12345 logical bytes, max single entry 8192, max expansion ratio 1500 milli, 7 Chunks, max path depth 4, max metadata 2048 bytes, max KDF cost 0.

DESCRIPTOR_V2_MAX is a canonical vector with every budget u64 and decode flags u32 set to all-ones, implying encoding-level acceptance of undefined decode-flag bits and maximal budgets; whether such values are semantically valid is unstated.
research_needed: Test reader behaviour with all-ones flags and budgets; define flag registry.

statement: PublicCryptoContext uses a distinct framing: u16 domain length, entrybound/public-crypto-context/v1, u16 field count (11), then fields as u16 tag plus u64 length plus value, without the record TLV type byte.

Public context vectors use archive_id 00..1f, INDEXED/Complete, BUCKETED padding, SECRET_GEAR_TABLE, X-Wing, feature bits 0x000f; legacy uses required features 0x04ef, Descriptor-v2 uses 0x14ef, the sole difference.

Decoded 0x04ef = 0x0f (cross-file compression, codec-transform, reconstructive, whole-object reconstruction) + encrypted-indexed + payload-suite + recipient-xwing + crypto-padding; PHTE bit 0x800 unset, so reconstruction features are exercised with encryption.

Because required feature bits (including 0x1000) are bound into the public crypto context, legacy Descriptor-v1 and corrected v2 encrypted archives have distinct authenticated contexts, presumably preventing downgrade between them.
research_needed: Formal analysis that the public context is bound into AEAD associated data/key derivation; downgrade attack tests.

statement: Public context fields 2-5 (2-byte values 0,1,1,1) and 10-11 (one-byte 01) are unlabelled in the vector file, so vectors are not self-describing for independent implementers.
